threads.body: [Testing] This test currently pre-populates AgentDistributionConfig from system properties only, so it doesn’t validate the declarative-config path described in the PR (i.e., parsing `distribution.javaagent.thread_details_enabled` via JavaagentDistributionAccessCustomizerProvider). That leaves the main integration between the distribution node and ThreadDetailsCustomizerProvider untested.

replies.body: Good catch — reworked the test to drive the full declarative-config path. It now parses YAML with `distribution.javaagent.thread_details_enabled` and runs `JavaagentDistributionAccessCustomizerProvider` (which populates `AgentDistributionConfig`) ahead of `ThreadDetailsCustomizerProvider`, so the distribution-node → customizer integration is actually exercised.

threads.body: To support the declarative-config coverage improvement above (applying multiple customizer providers), `applyCustomizer` should accept the `DeclarativeConfigurationCustomizerProvider` interface instead of the concrete `ThreadDetailsCustomizerProvider` type.

replies.body: Done — `applyCustomizers` now accepts `DeclarativeConfigurationCustomizerProvider...` and chains the providers in `order()`, which is what enabled the coverage improvement above.

threads.body: [Testing] `hasAttributesSatisfying(...)` is the non-exact attribute assertion variant, which (by design) ignores any unexpected attributes. Since this smoke test is only asserting presence/validity of `thread.id` and `thread.name`, using two `hasAttribute(satisfies(...))` calls keeps the intent clear and avoids the non-exact helper.

threads.body: [Testing] `propertyValue == null` is currently unreachable here: `@CsvSource` provides an empty string for the ", false" row (not `null`), so the ternary’s null branch never runs and the test doesn’t actually cover the “property not set” scenario it describes. Use `@CsvSource(nullValues = ...)` (or `@NullSource`) so the null case is exercised intentionally.

replies.body: Good catch — fixed with `@CsvSource(nullValues = "NULL")` so the null case is exercised intentionally. I kept both distinct false-paths covered: the `NULL` row (distribution node absent) and the empty-value row (`thread_details_enabled:` key present with no value, which parses to a null scalar).

threads.body: `processor.getAdditionalProperties()` is dereferenced without a null-check. Elsewhere in the model you already treat collections as nullable (e.g., `getProcessors()`), so this should defensively handle `null` to avoid a potential NPE when iterating existing processor models.

replies.body: Two things: (1) `getAdditionalProperties()` is non-null by contract — the jsonschema2pojo post-processing in opentelemetry-java adds `@Nullable` to every generated getter *except* `getAdditionalProperties` (regex `get(?!AdditionalProperties)`), and the map is always an initialized `LinkedHashMap`. (2) This method (`threadDetailsProcessorIsAlreadyConfigured`) was since removed — the dedup guard was dropped as over-engineering — so the code no longer exists at HEAD.

threads.body: `distribution.getAdditionalProperties()` is accessed without checking for null. If `additionalProperties` can be absent, this will throw at runtime; guard by reading the map into a local variable and returning `false` when it's null/missing.

replies.body: `getAdditionalProperties()` is non-null by contract. The declarative-config model POJOs are generated by jsonschema2pojo in opentelemetry-java, and the post-processing step adds `@Nullable` to every generated getter *except* `getAdditionalProperties` — the regex is `get(?!AdditionalProperties)` with the comment "Add @Nullable annotations to all getters (except getAdditionalProperties which is non-null)". The map is the catch-all bucket, always initialized to an empty `LinkedHashMap`. (Declared collections like `getProcessors()` *can* be null because the build sets `initializeCollections = false`, which is why those are guarded — but that does not apply to `additionalProperties`.) So `.get("spring_starter")` just returns null when absent, which the next line already handles.

threads.body: The component name `\"thread_details\"` is duplicated as a string literal in tests (and similarly in the Spring test). Prefer a shared constant (e.g., `AddThreadDetailsComponentProvider.NAME`) or at least a local `private static final String` to prevent drift if the component name ever changes.

replies.body: Good call — switched both tests to use `ThreadDetailsComponentProvider.NAME` instead of the hardcoded literal.

On reflection, reverted this — keeping the literal `"thread_details"` on purpose. It is the user-facing declarative-config YAML node name (a contract), so the test should pin it explicitly and fail if `NAME` is ever renamed, rather than tautologically tracking the production constant. Test independence is the priority here over avoiding drift.

threads.body: Adding the thread-details processor unconditionally can lead to duplicate `thread_details` span processors if the user already configured one in the declarative config. This can add unnecessary overhead (processor invoked twice per span) and differs from the existing span-logging customizer, which avoids installing duplicates.

replies.body: Intentional — the dedup guard was removed as over-engineering. A duplicate `thread_details` processor can only arise if a user hand-authors `thread_details:` in their config *and* enables the distro flag, which is a contrived self-misconfiguration for an internal, distro-gated feature that users are not expected to author directly. The span-logging customizer guards against duplicates because `console` is a genuinely user-facing exporter people add themselves; that likelihood does not carry over here.

threads.body:
[Performance] AbstractThreadDetailsCustomizerProvider always appends the `thread_details` span processor when enabled, even if the user already configured it in YAML (or if the customizer runs more than once). That can result in duplicate processors and extra per-span work.

Consider checking for an existing processor model with the `thread_details` additional property before adding a new one (similar to how AbstractSpanLoggingCustomizerProvider avoids installing a duplicate logging exporter).

This mismatch is likely to confuse reviewers/users reading the PR description.
